newsitem.title: VIRGIN ISLANDS: Murder rate doubles on US Virgin Island St. Croix.
newsitem.headline: Murder rate doubles on US Virgin Island St. Croix.

text.p: The murder rate on the Caribbean island of St. Croix has soared to twice last year's level and police said on Wednesday they were at a loss to explain the recent wave of violent crimes.

Within one week, the normally peaceful island, a favorite cruise ship destination, has seen the rape of a mentally disabled woman, five shootings and a murder. A police spokesman said the department was especially concerned because off-duty officers were under investigation in connection with one of the shootings.

On April 19, the estranged husband of a St. Croix police officer was apparently beaten with a bat and grazed in the head by a bullet. On April 21, three people were struck by gunfire in a drive-by shooting near a basketball court and another man was shot in the head in an unrelated incident.

The homicide occurred on April 18 when Sean Petersen, 28, brother of the territory's agriculture commissioner, Arthur Petersen, was stabbed to death. The mentally disabled woman was assaulted on April 19.
St. Croix has seen six homicides so far this year, twice last year's level. There have been 14 homicides this year in all of the Virgin Islands, a U.S. territory in the Caribbean.
